tasks.short: Agree the desired haircut with the patron

steps.what: Question patrons about desired services and haircut styles

tasks.design: Keep the consultation with the barber. A prior preference in {CRM} can prompt a question but cannot establish what the patron wants today.
tasks.previous_blocker: The requested style depends on the person and their hair.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change is needed for this conversation.
tasks.still_hard: A familiar style name can mean different lengths or finishes.
tasks.human_edge: The barber clarifies expectations while observing the hair.
tasks.altitude: The barber retains the same consultation responsibility.

reach.learn: Discuss care without promising an unsuitable result

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: observing hair and resolving a patron's preferences require a personal consultation.

assumptions: Boundary is the consultation, excluding booking, service delivery and later client-card entry.
No structured preference flag is assumed or produced automatically; the barber establishes the request in s1.
Test existing client-history access before adding software; existing runtime earns no saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because the conversation and its tools are unchanged.
unknowns: How often patrons bring usable reference photos
research_questions: Which questions most often prevent a misunderstood length request?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0; no consultation time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record delivered services and collect payment

steps.what: Select delivered services and authorised prices on the cashier ticket
Calculate totals and populate the cashier ticket in the till system
Check the ticket and receive payment from the customer

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} till system to calculate and populate a draft from the barber's selected service lines. The barber checks the amount, obtains payment and handles discrepancies before closing the ticket.
tasks.previous_blocker: A booking does not necessarily describe the services actually delivered.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing till calculations can reuse explicitly selected service lines.
tasks.still_hard: Discounts, changed services and disputed charges need a person.
tasks.human_edge: The barber explains the charge and resolves disagreement.
tasks.altitude: Less ticket arithmetic; payment responsibility stays with the barber.

reach.learn: Trace service lines and authorised discounts

evidence.claim: Salonized offers salon payments and a financial overview; this supports a native till option, not a measured saving.
Model knowledge: calculating a ticket from selected lines is deterministic; the proposed labour allocation requires a local timing study.

assumptions: Boundary is checkout; service delivery and customer payment effort are outside the focal denominator and unchanged.

The barber produces service code, quantity, approved unit price, currency, applicable tax category and authorised discount in s1; its 35 hours include capture and correction. Missing or disputed fields stop calculation and the barber prepares the ticket manually within exception upkeep.
Test the native till before code; count only observed manual arithmetic and duplicate ticket entry, not existing runtime.
Price-list maintenance and exceptional ticket correction add four focal hours per 100 baseline hours.
unknowns: Whether the till already performs all calculation
Frequency of nonstandard services and split payments
research_questions: Does a timed checkout sample contain the proposed 20% manual ticket-preparation work?

incremental.description: Price upkeep and manual ticket exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact ticket version, services, quantities, prices, discount, tax and total checked immediately before charging; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20 and net=16 after four upkeep hours. Range assumes only part of ticket arithmetic is currently manual; an already automated till yields no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep business records, pay bills and manage personnel

steps.what: Keep business records in the finance system
Check bills and approve their payment in the bank
Assess candidates and make hiring decisions
Supervise personnel and discuss work quality

tasks.design: Keep record checks, bill decisions, hiring and supervision with the barber. Inspect existing {ERP} and {BANK} configuration before proposing any separate copying tool; no manual rekeying baseline is established here.
tasks.previous_blocker: This broad duty mixes business judgement with record work of unknown volume.
tasks.enabler_now: Native finance and bank functions are available, but availability does not establish additional labour saving.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing whether a bill is valid and whether a candidate fits the salon.
tasks.human_edge: The barber accepts financial responsibility and coaches staff.
tasks.altitude: Decision rights and weekly responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Match bills and receipts to actual business events

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: hiring, supervision and bill validity depend on business context; native transaction handling alone does not remove those decisions.

assumptions: Boundary excludes client cards and checkout owned by the other tasks; the four shares are a provisional broad-duty split, not measured local data.

Supplier produces the invoice and existing bank workflow produces a payment draft before s2; barber verifies payee, account, invoice identity, amount and due date in the counted 25 hours. Missing data is resolved manually; no new structured producer or machine step is claimed.
Try native finance configuration first; existing calculations and bank runtime do not earn savings.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new process or integration is introduced.
unknowns: The actual split between bookkeeping, bills and people management
Any duplicate data entry between till and ledger
research_questions: Does observed record work contain a distinct repeated transfer worth changing?

approvals.approved_version: Exact bank draft payee, account, invoice, amount, currency and execution date reviewed in s2; any change requires fresh approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and net=0. No duplicate transfer has been established and all four duties retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain the client card after each visit

steps.what: Record work done and products used against the client's visit
Copy fees and file the visit notes in the client card
Check the client card for accurate work, products and fees

tasks.design: Use native {CRM} client cards to file the barber's notes and reuse the linked checkout fee. The barber still records actual products used and checks the finished card; purchases cannot stand in for treatment details.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate tickets and client cards require duplicate fee entry and filing.
tasks.enabler_now: Client-card software can hold visit notes and treatment or purchase history together.
tasks.still_hard: Identifying the right client and recording what actually happened.
tasks.human_edge: The barber recognises details relevant to the next visit.
tasks.altitude: More time remembering the client and less copying fee information.

reach.learn: Check identity and distinguish treatment from purchase history

evidence.claim: Salonized client management supports paperless client cards with treatment and purchase history and appointment or treatment notes.
Model knowledge: reusing an identified checkout fee avoids copying without inferring treatment details.

assumptions: Boundary begins after checkout; payment and general business records are counted elsewhere.

Barber produces client ID, visit ID, date, work description, actual products used and checked ticket ID in s1; all capture and association cost is in its 40 hours. Checkout task produces ticket ID, fee, currency and payment state before this task. Missing identity or link requires manual card entry, included in upkeep; no inference from a booking or purchase list.
Test native linked client cards before custom integration; savings require observed duplicate copying and filing, not existing runtime.
Keep only necessary service notes; any new sensitive-data collection requires a separate local decision and is not assumed.
unknowns: Whether checkout and client card already share an identifier
research_questions: Can a sample of actual visits be linked without increasing misfiled cards?

already_counted.description: Capture actual treatment details and confirm the ticket link

incremental.description: Correct missing links and maintain card fields

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60, gross=40 and net=35 after five upkeep hours. Range assumes partial duplicate fee entry and filing; already-linked cards have little or no additional saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep the consultation and people decisions personal while checking a smaller amount of duplicated checkout and record work.
reach: Resolve routine reception ticket and client-record discrepancies
skills_to_grow: Link visits without confusing client identities
role.ambitious_version: A barber who retains time for patron conversations while maintaining reliable visit history.
